title: Sharp moment bounds for reversible negative eigenfunctions and spectral graph homomorphisms
oneLine: A sharp limit on positive–negative moment imbalance extends a known spectral graph-mapping obstruction beyond square energies.
abstract: A reversible process can have a balanced average while its positive and negative higher moments differ. This candidate proves a sharp comparison for exchangeable pairs with exact negative linear regression, valid for every real exponent at least two, and determines the universal positive-exponent range. A spectral-projector reduction transfers the result to positive unital self-adjoint maps and strict vector colourings. It extends the known square-energy homomorphism bound to all real exponents above two for edge-transitive targets. The paper includes explicit extremisers, reversible-chain counterexamples below two, residual-error estimates and an inherited 1-walk-regular target corollary. The stronger ordinary-vector conjecture and the graph exponent classification below two remain unresolved here.

keyResults: For exact negative regression E[Y|X]=−rX, the positive and negative p-moments differ by at most r^(1−p), sharply for every p≥2.
The universal positive-exponent range for all admissible reversible pairs is {1} union [2,infinity); this is not a graph exponent classification.
Positive-map reduction yields the strict-vector/theta bound for p≥2; p>2 is the graph extension beyond known square-energy results.
Edge-transitive homomorphism obstructions extend to all p≥2, with an elementary 1-walk-regular target corollary using an established colouring construction.
Complex Hermitian and controlled residual formulations are elementary consequences; the ordinary-vector conjecture remains open here.

narration:
Averages can balance while large fluctuations do not. This unrefereed, AI-assisted research candidate asks how uneven those fluctuations can become in a reversible random process.

Reversible means that, in equilibrium, a pair of successive observations has the same distribution when its order is reversed. Suppose also that the expected next observation is a negative fraction of the current one. A positive value therefore predicts a negative average next step, and vice versa.

The paper bounds the imbalance between positive and negative moments: averages of powers of their magnitudes. For every real exponent at least two, it gives an exact limit determined by that negative fraction.

A two-state example makes the bound tangible. One state has value one. The other has value minus one half. From the positive state, the process always moves to the negative state. From the negative state, it either returns or stays, with equal probabilities.

In equilibrium, the positive state occurs one third of the time. The negative state occurs two thirds. Their contributions to the ordinary signed average cancel. But their cubic moments do not. The positive cubic moment is one third; the negative cubic moment is one twelfth. That is a ratio of four, exactly attaining the new bound.

The proof also determines the universal exponent range for these reversible pairs. That classification does not automatically extend to graphs.

The graph application concerns spectral energies: sums of powers of positive and negative adjacency eigenvalues. It extends a known square-energy homomorphism bound to every real exponent above two, for graphs mapping into an edge-transitive target. A related bound uses strict vector colourings. The stronger conjecture about ordinary vector colourings remains unresolved here.

The general result rests on a written mathematical argument. Finite examples and internal AI review provide supplementary checks, not external peer review or formal proof verification. Historical priority also remains subject to the limits of the source search.
